title: From Supervised to Generative: A Novel Paradigm for Tabular Deep Learning with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Tabular predictive modeling requires models that can transfer knowledge, generalize from limited data, and follow human instructions across diverse industries.

gap.claim: Current tabular deep learning approaches have not fully addressed the demand for universal models with these capabilities.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Generative Tabular Learning, a framework that integrates prompt-based zero-shot generalization and in-context learning from large language models into tabular deep learning.
The framework provides a training resource and test bed for improving large language models' comprehension of tabular data.
The authors release code, data, and model checkpoints.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Generative Tabular Learning as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The empirical study covers 384 public datasets and analyzes convergence, scaling behavior, and the effects of different data templates.
The GTL-enhanced LLaMA-2 model demonstrates zero-shot and in-context learning capabilities across classification and regression tasks.
Without fine-tuning, the model reportedly outperforms traditional methods and rivals GPT-4 in some cases.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular data supports predictive modeling in multiple crucial industries.
The field increasingly needs universal models that transfer knowledge, generalize from limited data, and follow human instructions, while current approaches have not fully met these needs.
The authors introduce GTL, integrating LLM capabilities into tabular deep learning and leveraging LLM pre-training on diverse tabular data.
The study evaluates GTL across 384 public datasets, including convergence, scaling, data templates, classification, and regression.
The authors report strong zero-shot and in-context performance without fine-tuning, along with released code, data, and checkpoints.

source_observation.claim: Pre-training on diverse tabular data is described as supporting understanding of domain knowledge, numerical sequences, and statistical dependencies.

interpretation.claim: Broad tabular pre-training may help a general-purpose model transfer across tabular domains and tasks.

application.claim: When designing tabular foundation models, consider pre-training data diversity and representations of numerical and statistical structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which pre-training choices cause the reported gains or how performance varies across domains.

source_observation.claim: The reported results indicate zero-shot and in-context capabilities without fine-tuning across classification and regression tasks.

interpretation.claim: A single tabular model may support task adaptation through prompting rather than task-specific parameter updates.

application.claim: For limited-data tabular workflows, evaluate prompting and in-context learning as alternatives or complements to fine-tuning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the task distributions, baselines, prompting procedures, or cases where fine-tuning remains necessary.

unknowns: Specific model architecture and training procedure are not described.
Dataset identities, splits, metrics, baselines, and statistical results are not provided.
The conditions and scope of the reported comparison with GPT-4 are unspecified.
The released resource contents and licensing are unspecified.
